title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
why_read: A creative and rigorous benchmark comparing LLM and embedding-model navigation ability against humans on a well-defined graph traversal task.
analysis: The paper uses the Wikipedia Game, where players must navigate from one article to a target using only hyperlinks, as a proxy for testing how well language models can do multi-hop information retrieval over huge, unindexed document graphs. They test both embedding models and LLMs across five languages and extend the idea to academic citation graphs built from OpenAlex data. The finding that no model clearly beats human performance, with top models like GPT-o3 mini and DeepSeek-R1 only matching humans, is a useful calibration point for anyone using LLMs for literature or knowledge-base search. The released code for building and navigating these graphs without relying on third-party APIs is a practical contribution for reproducible research.
